report.source_text: The computed tomography (CT) of the thorax, abdomen, and pelvis revealed the presence of a 23/19 mm (transverse) and 20 mm (cranial–caudal) mass lesion, respectively, having speculated margins, contrast enhancement, and areas of necrosis at the level of the dorsal segment of the right upper pulmonary lobe. The mass presented several extensions to the pleura and determined pleural invasion (Figs. 5 and 6). In addition, multiple mediastinal adenopathy were noticed, and some of them presented central necrosis. No oncologic abnormalities were found at the examination of the abdomen and pelvis. Also, the cerebral CT scan did not show any pathological findings.

clinician.final_diagnosis: pulmonary adenocarcinoma with lymph nodes metastases and paraneoplastic hypertrophic osteoarthropathy
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 41-year-old heavy smoker presented with pain, joint swelling, clubbing of fingers and toes, enlarged joints, swollen tubular extremities, and pachydermia, highly suggestive of hypertrophic osteoarthropathy. A CT scan of the thorax, abdomen, and pelvis revealed a 23/19 mm lung mass in the dorsal segment of the right upper pulmonary lobe with speculated margins, contrast enhancement, necrosis, and pleural invasion. Multiple mediastinal adenopathies, some with central necrosis, were also noted. No other oncologic abnormalities were found in the abdomen, pelvis, or brain. Histological confirmation of the lung mass and lymph node metastases was attempted but the results were not successfully retrieved.

key_supporting_evidence.claim: Patient presented with symptoms consistent with hypertrophic osteoarthropathy, including clubbing of fingers and toes, enlarged large joints, swollen tubular extremities, and pachydermia.
CT scan revealed a 23/19 mm lung mass in the dorsal segment of the right upper pulmonary lobe with speculated margins, contrast enhancement, necrosis, and pleural invasion.
CT scan showed multiple mediastinal adenopathy, some with central necrosis.

ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.alternative: Metastatic disease to abdomen, pelvis, or brain
ruled_out_or_less_likely_alternatives.basis: No oncologic abnormalities found at the examination of the abdomen and pelvis, and cerebral CT scan did not show any pathological findings (E005)

remaining_uncertainties: Histological confirmation of pulmonary adenocarcinoma from the lung mass biopsy
Histological confirmation of lymph node metastases from the mediastinal adenopathy biopsy
